newsitem.title: JAPAN: COFFEE - Ample stocks keep Japan calm despite rally.
newsitem.headline: COFFEE - Ample stocks keep Japan calm despite rally.

text.p: Japan's coffee traders said on Friday they need not panic about skyrocketing global market prices, because domestic coffee stocks are ample.
Local roasters increased their wholesale prices from May to reflect rising market prices, but they said they have no plans to raise prices further at the moment.
On Thursday, the New York coffee futures market rallied to 20-year highs as speculators led a buying frenzy amid a background of tight supplies.
The spot May contract soared 15.55 cents to 277.05 cents, after peaking at 279.00 cents, its highest price since 1977.
"Recent coffee prices are beyond our expectations. I can't imagine what will come next," a coffee trader at a major trade house said.
"But we are not concerned about possible supply shortages here at the moment because local coffee stocks are increasing steadily," he said.

Coffee stocks at Japanese warehouses totalled 67,030 tonnes at the end of March, up by 26.7 percent from a year earlier, according to Agriculture Ministry data. End-of-April coffee stock data will be available later this month.
Of the end-March stocks, Brazilian and Colombian coffee amounted to 14,187 tonnes and 14,669 tonnes respectively.
Stocks of Indonesian beans were 11,051 tonnes.

Some traders said North American and European coffee traders were likely to rush to buy robusta coffee from Indonesia and Vietnam, because of the cheaper price compared with arabica beans produced in Latin America.
"Their rush to buy robusta beans may push prices higher," said another coffee trader in Tokyo. "We're thinking of buying more robusta from Asian producers before that happens."
Robusta coffee is mainly used to make ice coffee in Japan, a popular drink during the summer. Demand for ice coffee usually grows when summer temperatures are above normal levels.
Major roaster UCC Ueshima Coffee Co Ltd, which raised wholesale coffee prices by about 20 percent from this month, said it currently had no plans to raise prices further.

"We're aware of the world coffee market's rally, but we would like to wait-and-see the market for a while," a UCC spokesman said. "The yen's gains against the dollar have partly offset the rise in coffee prices," he said.
The U.S. dollar has fallen from levels of nearly 127 yen at the beginning of this month to about 116 yen this afternoon.
Japan's total green coffee imports in the first three months of this year totalled 85,784 tonnes, against 65,834 tonnes the previous year, according to the latest Finance Ministry data.
Japan is the world's third-largest coffee consumer after the United States and Germany.
